title: Stable influence at parameter one
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$, and let $i$ be a coordinate. At parameter $1$, the stable influence of $f$ at $i$ equals its influence at $i$, where influence is the uniform average of the square of the discrete derivative $[f(x^{i,+})-f(x^{i,-})]/2$; here $x^{i,+}$ and $x^{i,-}$ are obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $1$ and $-1$, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
